title: Recursive shelves: Peak ticket
topics: Recursion, sorting, binary search and bits
summary: Divide-and-conquer recursion. Return the largest number.
descriptionMd:
Inputs
`readings` is a list of integers (numbers with no decimal part). It may be empty, and numbers may repeat unless task 1 says otherwise.

Your tasks
1. Create a list `sectionSums`. Start with the whole `readings` list as a section. Record the sum of that section. If it has more than one number, split it into a left half and a right half. Use the same steps on the left half first, then on the right half. When a section has an odd length, the left half has one fewer number. A section with one number is not split. Do not record empty sections. `sectionSums` contains the sums in the order you record them.
2. Find the largest number in `sectionSums`. Store it in `largest`.
3. Complete `recursiveShelvesPeakTicket` so it returns `largest`. Return it, do not print it.

Example
If `readings` is [4, 3, -4, 4, 0], then `sectionSums` is [7, 7, 4, 3, 0, -4, 4, 4, 0] and `recursiveShelvesPeakTicket` returns 7.

Rules
- If `sectionSums` is empty, return 0.
- If every number is negative, return the largest negative number. Do not replace it with 0.

Test data
TEST DATA 1: `readings` is [0, 13, 4, -9, 4].
TEST DATA 2: `readings` is [4, 4, -7, 4].

Efficiency goal: time O(n log n); extra memory, including the helper list, O(n). n is the input length. These labels describe how work and memory grow with the input.
